paragraphs: On Saturday afternoon, it rained, and Tom and Lily stayed at home. Pip lay on a cushion next to the sofa. "You can watch TV for one hour," said Mom. "Please choose one program together." Tom turned on the TV, and Lily sat next to him.

"I want to watch a comedy," said Tom. "My reason is simple: I like funny things, and I laugh a lot." "I want a pop show," said Lily. "My reason is that I like the songs, and the dancers are good." "A pop show is too loud for me," said Tom. "Does it bother you?" asked Lily. "Yes, a little, because I like to hear the words," said Tom.

"Let's watch the comedy first for thirty minutes," said Lily. "Then we can watch the pop show." "That is fair," said Tom. "My opinion is that two programs are better than one." They watched the comedy, and Tom laughed until he held his side. Pip lifted his head, looked at the TV, and put his head down again.

During the pop show, Tom said, "I got an email from Alex yesterday." "Alex has a new game, and he likes it a lot." "In the game, you need a license before you drive a car." "A license in a game is a good idea," said Lily. "It is like a real test, and it is also a bit funny." "I do not like level three," said Tom. "It is impossible to finish it in one hour." "That is not a game for one hour," said Lily with a smile.

Mom came in with two cups of tea. "What is your opinion about my rule?" she asked. "One hour for TV is a good set of rules for a rainy day," said Lily. "My reason is that I want to read my book, too." "I think it is a little short," said Tom, "but I agree." "I have homework, and one hour is enough." Mom smiled and gave them the tea. "I like your reasons," she said.

When the hour ended, Tom turned off the TV. Pip stood up and walked to the door, because he wanted to go out. "It is still raining, Pip," said Lily. She took her book and sat on the sofa. The rain made a soft sound on the roof, and the room was warm.
text.summary: On a rainy Saturday, Mom gives Tom and Lily one hour of screen time. They give their opinions about a comedy, a pop show, a game, and Mom's rule, and each one gives a reason.

sentences.text: On Saturday afternoon, it rained, and Tom and Lily stayed at home.
Pip lay on a cushion next to the sofa.
"You can watch TV for one hour," said Mom.
"Please choose one program together."
Tom turned on the TV, and Lily sat next to him.
"I want to watch a comedy," said Tom.
"My reason is simple: I like funny things, and I laugh a lot."
"I want a pop show," said Lily.
"My reason is that I like the songs, and the dancers are good."
"A pop show is too loud for me," said Tom.
"Does it bother you?" asked Lily.
"Yes, a little, because I like to hear the words," said Tom.
"Let's watch the comedy first for thirty minutes," said Lily.
"Then we can watch the pop show."
"That is fair," said Tom.
"My opinion is that two programs are better than one."
They watched the comedy, and Tom laughed until he held his side.
Pip lifted his head, looked at the TV, and put his head down again.
During the pop show, Tom said, "I got an email from Alex yesterday."
"Alex has a new game, and he likes it a lot."
"In the game, you need a license before you drive a car."
"A license in a game is a good idea," said Lily.
"It is like a real test, and it is also a bit funny."
"I do not like level three," said Tom.
"It is impossible to finish it in one hour."
"That is not a game for one hour," said Lily with a smile.
Mom came in with two cups of tea.
"What is your opinion about my rule?" she asked.
"One hour for TV is a good set of rules for a rainy day," said Lily.
"My reason is that I want to read my book, too."
"I think it is a little short," said Tom, "but I agree."
"I have homework, and one hour is enough."
Mom smiled and gave them the tea.
"I like your reasons," she said.
When the hour ended, Tom turned off the TV.
Pip stood up and walked to the door, because he wanted to go out.
"It is still raining, Pip," said Lily.
She took her book and sat on the sofa.
The rain made a soft sound on the roof, and the room was warm.
